uncovered_surfaces: §11.2 default-material color chain + brightness clamp [0,8]: 'final_linear = base × tint × brightness' with silent clamp outside [0,8] (never an error) is a CPU-resolvable §11.2 numeric surface and has NO test. The plan assumes the whole default-material/lighting chain is P1, but §11.2 (a P3 section) pins the clamp rule and the linear color-chain math. No task exposes a CPU accessor for the default-material effective_diffuse/brightness clamp nor asserts the clamp boundary (e.g. brightness=9 clamps to 8, brightness=-1 clamps to 0, never errors).

§11.3 default-material-lit-by-registered-lights forward loop: §11.3 says 'default-material nodes respond to registered lights through the SAME forward lighting loop as PBR'. T10/T11 test only light SELECTION (default_light_active bool, selected/dropped node ids) — no task asserts that a default-material node's CPU-resolvable shading actually responds to a registered light (no CPU lighting reference fn analogous to the tonemap CPU reference in T14). The behavioral surface 'default material is lit ONLY by registered lights once a Light is in subtree' is asserted as a flag, not as a shading result.

§11.4 unknown render.msaa value vs unknown enc/feat: covered. But §11.4 'msaa= supported set {2,8} only where adapter reports support' — the adapter-reports-support branch (2/8 advertised) is never exercised; P3-T2 fixes baseline {1,4} for GPU-free tests and never tests the path where the cap list grows to include 2/8 (acceptable for GPU-free, but the {2,8} advertisement surface is uncovered).

§7.1 feat= token 'pbr' implication is tested (T2) but the §7.1 implication 'anim ⇒ graph' and the full frozen v1 feat vocabulary are out of P3 scope — fine. However P3-T2 asserts feat= contains material+pbr+light but does NOT assert the §7.1 ordering/closed-set property that the terminal MUST NOT advertise a token without its implied token in the SAME reply across the P3-added tokens only (covered loosely). Minor.

issues.problem: P3-T17 VRAM formula contradicts §11.1/§10.4. The plan charges the MSAA resolve target as pixels×1×(color_bytes+depth_bytes), i.e. it INCLUDES depth in the resolve target. But §11.1 line 19 states 'MSAA resolve (color target only)' and §11.4 confirms 'the MSAA resolve apply only to the color target'. The resolve target carries NO depth. The correct charge is: MSAA target = pixels×samples×(color+depth); resolve target = pixels×1×color (color ONLY); pick target = pixels×1×(color+depth) when active. The plan over-charges every multisampled viewport by one full-resolution depth buffer, making tgp_viewport_vram() disagree with the honest cap the design promises to advertise.
issues.fix: Rewrite P3-T17's deliverable formula and the test 'vram_charge_includes_msaa_multiplier_resolve_and_pick' to: pixels×samples×(color+depth) [msaa] + pixels×1×color [resolve, COLOR ONLY per §11.1] + pixels×1×(color+depth) [pick, when active]. Assert the resolve term excludes depth.

issues.problem: P3-T14's tone_map-unknown-operator test is a vague/placeholder assertion. It says assert 'tgp;x;vp=2;code=bad_param;detail=tone_map (or documented silent-None — assert the chosen §11.4 behavior)'. This is two mutually exclusive behaviors with the concrete expected value left undecided ('assert the chosen behavior'). §11.4 explicitly frames tone_map and msaa as quality knobs (msaa silently clamps, never errors); the plan itself uses silent-clamp for msaa (T15) but leaves tone_map's unknown-value behavior unresolved, contradicting its own quality-knob treatment. A reviewer cannot tell what the terminal must emit.
issues.fix: Decide ONE behavior consistent with §11.4's quality-knob framing. Recommended: unknown render.tone_map silently defaults to None (parity with msaa silent-clamp; quality knob not a resource), and the test asserts Term::tgp_viewport_render_opts(vp).tone_map == ToneMap::None with NO tgp;x emitted. If instead bad_param is chosen, drop the 'or' and assert the exact bytes. Eliminate the 'assert the chosen behavior' wording.

issues.problem: P3-T3/T4 assert material.add re-add → x;code=dup_id and 'materials immutable once committed (remove+add)', but the design does NOT state material immutability. §8.4's collision rule covers only ASSETS ('add on an existing committed ASSET id is an error (dup_id); assets are immutable'). §8.6/§8.4 never declare materials immutable; material.add is a distinct op and there is no node.remove-equivalent for materials described, nor a material.remove op. The plan invents both material immutability AND the remove+add replacement path with no design basis. dup_id is in the closed enum so it is a legal code, but applying it to materials is an unverified extrapolation.
issues.fix: Flag for design confirmation. Either (a) add an explicit design line in §8.4/§8.6 making materials immutable-once-committed with dup_id on re-add and naming the replacement path (is there a material.remove? assets use node.remove cascades but materials are not nodes), then keep T4; or (b) if materials are intended to be mutable via re-add (sparse-merge like node.upsert), change T4 to assert the merge semantics instead of dup_id. As written the test asserts behavior the design does not specify.

issues.problem: P3-T5 has a self-contradicting error-mapping for oversize textures. §11.2 is unambiguous: 'A texture exceeding max_tex_dim ... is rejected with tgp;x;code=parse_error (detail=tex_dim)'. The plan's deliverable text says 'TexError::DimExceeded→(parse_error, detail=tex_dim) for hard-reject AND cap_exceeded;detail=max_tex_dim for the cap locus' then walks it back to 'follow §11.2 wording: rejected with parse_error detail=tex_dim'. Carrying the cap_exceeded;detail=max_tex_dim alternative at all is wrong — §15.2/§15.5 route texture-dimension over-cap through parse_error;detail=tex_dim (texture decode locus), not cap_exceeded. Leaving the dual mapping invites an implementer to emit the wrong code.
issues.fix: Delete the cap_exceeded;detail=max_tex_dim mapping from P3-T5/T6 entirely. Oversize-dimension → parse_error;detail=tex_dim (whole-txn reject). Reserve cap_exceeded only where §15.5 uses it for texture decode: the decompression-bomb / running-output-over-budget locus (texels expansion) → cap_exceeded. Make P3-T5's 'png_over_max_texels' and 'decompression_bomb' tests assert the code each path actually uses, and keep 'png_over_max_tex_dim' on parse_error;detail=tex_dim.

issues.problem: P3-T5/T6 confuse max_texels_per_texture (the header/decoded texel-count cap, §7.1/§15.2) with the incremental decode-budget guard (§15.5 'abort if running output exceeds the budget'). The plan treats over-max_texels as a header-time TexelsExceeded AND the decompression-bomb as a separate bounded-decode abort, but does not state which CODE the texels-over-cap path emits. §11.2/§15.5 reject by parse_error for format/dim; the texels-expansion-over-budget locus in §15.5 emits cap_exceeded. The 'png_over_max_texels' test asserts only 'returns TexError::TexelsExceeded' (an internal enum) with no mapped wire code, and the asset.add wrapper (T6) never has a texels-over-cap ingress test asserting the emitted tgp;x code/detail.
issues.fix: Pin the wire mapping: header-declared texels > max_texels_per_texture → cap_exceeded;detail=max_texels_per_texture (per §7.1/§15.2 advertised-cap-name-in-detail rule), and add a P3-T6 ingress test feeding an asset.add fmt=png whose IHDR declares texels over cap, asserting pty_replies contains tgp;x;txn=..;code=cap_exceeded;detail=max_texels_per_texture and tgp_texture==None. Keep dim→parse_error;detail=tex_dim distinct.

issues.problem: P3-T2 advertises max_texels_per_texture but the cap is NOT in the reconciliation spine's enumerated cap list (G7 lists max_tex_dim but omits max_texels_per_texture). §7.1 and §15.2 DO list max_texels_per_texture=67108864, so the section files include it; G7 is stale/incomplete. The plan asserts the §7.1 value (67108864) which is correct, but because G7 (which 'wins' on conflict) omits the cap, an implementer following G7 would not advertise/enforce it, and §15.2's 'MUST NOT enforce a cap it did not advertise' would then forbid the texels check. The plan does not flag this G7-vs-§7.1 discrepancy.
issues.fix: Note the discrepancy explicitly in the phase notes and confirm max_texels_per_texture is advertised (it is in §7.1/§15.2, the authoritative section files; G7's list is non-exhaustive prose). Ensure P3-T2's reply serializer and Term::tgp_caps() include it. No test change needed but the plan should call out that it is relying on §7.1/§15.2 over G7's shorter list.

issues.problem: P3-T2/T15 muddle the MSAA-ack gating. §11.4 says the effective msaa is reported via the viewport ack 'when the app subscribed to acks'; G4 (which wins) says 'Acks are available to ANY handshaked token (not gated on sub)'. There is no 'ack subscription' concept. P3-T15's deliverable says 'reported via the viewport ack ONLY when the app subscribed to acks (any handshaked token, per G4)' — self-contradictory. The test 'msaa_effective_reported_in_ack' uses a handshaked token (correct) but the gate description is wrong and could lead to an implementation that requires a (nonexistent) ack subscription.
issues.fix: Restate the gate as: the msaa ack is emitted to any HANDSHAKED token (per G4), never gated on sub. Add a negative test: a tokenless/never-handshaked writer's vp frame with clamped msaa produces NO tgp;a (gating on handshake), mirroring the tokenless negative test in T12.

issues.problem: P3-T14 invents the wire spelling of the tone_map operator value (render.tone_map=aces / reinhard / none). §11.4 names the operators 'none / Reinhard / ACES' but does not fix the wire token casing. The plan asserts lowercase 'aces' without flagging it as an invented spelling, risking a mismatch if the design later pins 'ACES'.
issues.fix: Note that 'none|reinhard|aces' (lowercase) is a plan-chosen wire spelling pending design confirmation, and make the decode case-handling explicit (case-insensitive, or pinned lowercase) so the test's input bytes (render.tone_map=aces) are authoritative.

issues.problem: P3-T9 invents the light selector wire shape light:{type:directional,color:[...],intensity:...} including the field name 'type' and the kind sub-values 'directional/point/spot'. §8.6 confirms 'light' is a valid kind selector and §11.3 says 'KHR_lights_punctual style: directional/point/spot, color+intensity', but the CBOR sub-structure (key 'type' vs 'kind', spelling of the three kinds, range/spot-angle field names) is not specified anywhere in the section files. The plan asserts these without flagging them as invented.
issues.fix: Mark the light-selector CBOR schema (type key, directional|point|spot spelling, range, spot_inner/outer field names) as plan-defined pending design confirmation, since §11.3 leaves the wire encoding open. Keep the tests but note the schema is load-bearing on this choice.

issues.problem: P3-T16's interaction tests ('cpu_pick_unaffected_by_tone_map', 'cpu_pick_unaffected_by_msaa') depend on the P2 interaction seam (synthetic pointer via Term input API, deterministic clock, tgp;e click emission) but P3-T16 depends_on only [P3-T15, P3-T14, P2-cpu-picking]. The click-deadzone / explore controller and the tgp;e emission path that these tests assert ('resulting tgp;e;ev=click;node=... identical') are P2 surfaces; the plan does not call out that the deterministic-clock advance and the sub-must-be-active precondition are required for these interaction tests to be runnable.
issues.fix: Add P2 dependencies for the event-emission/sub path and the injectable clock to P3-T16 (e.g. P2-sub-events, P1-clock), and state in the test that a live sub on the viewport is established first and the clock is advanced explicitly before injecting the click, so the tgp;e assertion is well-defined.

issues.problem: P3-T13 theme_tint reads 'the terminal's active DEFAULT-FOREGROUND color'. §11.2 specifies 'the active default foreground color ... not one of the 16 ANSI indices and not the background'. The plan's test 'theme_tint_multiplies_fg_into_default_material' sets 'terminal default fg set to a known color' but does not specify the seam by which the test sets the terminal default fg (it is a Term/grid attribute, not a tgp frame), nor that it must be the default-fg specifically (not a SGR-set fg). Risk of asserting against the wrong fg source.
issues.fix: Specify the concrete seam to set the terminal default foreground for the test (e.g. config/theme default fg, or an OSC 10 sequence via Parser::advance), and assert that an SGR-set fg (CSI 3x m) does NOT feed theme-tint — only the default fg does, per §11.2.

notes: Overall the plan is strong: it correctly scopes to greenfield tgp/* trees (G8 clean break), keeps all geometry/material/light state CPU-side and queryable, uses the ingress seam for nearly everything with concrete CBOR/APC input bytes and concrete &self-accessor assertions, adds enc=bin variant tests sharing the CBOR path, and correctly notes the apc_end back-channel was a P1 change unchanged here (verified: perform.rs:42 still returns unit today). The sRGB math the plan asserts is verified against the existing render/src/color.rs inverse: linear_to_srgb_u8(0.5)==188, srgb_u8_to_lin(188) round-trips to 188, endpoints 0→0.0 and 255→1.0 exact — so P3-T1's tests are concrete and correct. The cap values (max_tex_dim=8192, max_texels_per_texture=67108864, max_lights_per_viewport=16, msaa=1,4) match §7.1 exactly; 8192x8193 correctly exceeds the texel cap (8192^2 == cap). Dependency ordering is buildable: color/caps first (T1,T2), then material table (T3,T4), texture decode (T5) before asset.add-png (T6) and GLB-embedded (T7), binding (T8) after both material and texture, lights (T9) → per-viewport selection (T10) → keep_default_light/over-cap (T11) → latch (T12), then the render-stage tasks (T13 theme-tint, T14 tone-map, T15 msaa, T16 pick-1x, T17 vram) and RIS teardown (T18) last. Clean-break, per-token isolation (T8 cross_token_material_ref_denied → denied;detail=token matches §8.4), deterministic clock (T12 advances render tick explicitly), CPU-resolvable pick, and pick-target-always-1x (T16) are all honored. \n\nBlocking before this phase is implementation-ready: P3-I1 (VRAM resolve over-charge contradicts §11.1 'resolve = color target only') and P3-I2 (tone_map unknown-operator test is a placeholder with no committed expected value). Also resolve the material-immutability design gap (P3-I3) and the texture error-code mappings (P3-I4, P3-I5) — these determine which closed-enum code/detail the terminal must emit and currently carry wrong or dual mappings (oversize-dim must be parse_error;detail=tex_dim per §11.2, NOT cap_exceeded). The §11.2 default-material brightness clamp [0,8] and the §11.3 'default material lit by registered lights' forward-loop behavior are genuine §11 surfaces with no test (uncovered_surfaces) — at minimum add a CPU-accessor + boundary test for the brightness clamp, since it is a concrete numeric CPU-resolvable surface with explicit silent-clamp semantics. Several invented wire spellings (tone_map values, light selector CBOR schema) are reasonable but should be flagged as plan-defined pending design confirmation since the section files leave the encodings open.
